AccentMode.description:
How the accent colour behaves over time.

Every non-`Static` mode is a paid perk AND a moving element in the app shell, which this codebase
has repeatedly found to be expensive. Implementations must step on a timer (never per animation
frame), pause while the tab is hidden, and collapse to `Static` under
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

AccentSpeed.description:
How fast a moving accent moves.

A bounded set rather than a number, and the bound is the point: this drives a colour that changes
under the whole interface, and an arbitrary "speed" field would let somebody configure a strobe.
Even `Brisk` is slow enough that a full spectrum lap takes about a minute.

AccessClaims.description: Claims carried by a user **access token** (short-lived JWT, signed by the Hub).

handle.description: Handle at issue time (convenience; authoritative value lives in the directory).

kid.description: Key id used to sign - lets the verifier select the right JWKS key during rotation.

sid.description:
Session id this token belongs to (ties the token to a device session so it can be listed /
revoked). Optional for backward compatibility with tokens minted before sessions existed.

AccountInfo.description:
Read-only account overview for the settings Account/Security tabs (`GET /v1/me/account`).
Deliberately separate from `UserProfile`, which is hand-built in several places and returned
from several endpoints — widening it has a far larger blast radius than a dedicated DTO.

email.description: The account's email address. `None` for accounts created without one (e.g. OAuth-only).

has_password.description: Whether a password credential exists, so the UI offers "change" vs. "set" a password.

passkey_count.description:
Number of registered passkeys. **Always 0 until passkeys ship**; it exists now so the
Security tab's shape does not change if they ever do.

AdminActivity.description:
What they are doing.

`dau`/`wau`/`mau` are distinct-listener counts over the trailing 1/7/30 days, read from the daily
rollup — never from `listening_events`, which is the partitioned fact table and the one thing an
admin refresh must not scan.

AdminBadgeUpdate.description:
`PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id}/badges`.

Three-valued per field, matching `UpdateProfile`: absent leaves it alone, `""` clears it, a value
sets it. Without that distinction an admin could not remove a developer title without also
clearing the staff role in the same request.

staff_role.description: `support` | `moderator` | `admin`, or `""` to remove the staff badge.

translator_languages.description:
The languages this person has translated, or `""` to remove the translator badge. Absent
leaves it alone, the same three-valued convention the fields above use.

AdminCatalog.description: What is in the catalog, and how much of the fleet is reachable.

AdminDayPoint.description:
One day of hub-wide activity.

`listeners` is what separates a busy day from one heavy listener, and it cannot be derived from
`plays` — which is exactly why it is a column here rather than something the client computes.

day.description: Local calendar day, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A DATE read as text: this crate's sqlx has no chrono.

AdminEnrichmentBacklog.description: How much of the catalog is still waiting on an enrichment worker.

AdminOverview.description: The Overview tab's whole payload, in one request.

AdminPlanGrantView.description: A live comp, as the admin user page shows it.

AdminRollupStat.description: One background rollup and how far behind it is.

lag_seconds.description: How far behind the newest event this rollup has processed, in seconds.

long_lived.description: A long-lived token — a paired device rather than a browser sign-in.

user_agent.description:
Raw UA string. Rendered as-is: parsing it into "Chrome on macOS" is a guess, and an operator
chasing a suspicious session wants the actual header.

AdminSignupPoint.description: One day of signups, for the growth chart.

AdminSystemHealth.description: Operator health, everything an admin would otherwise reach for psql to answer.

AdminTableSize.description: A table and what it costs on disk.

AdminTopEntity.description: A hub-wide top entity, with enough to render it as more than a name.

image_url.description:
A Hub-relative path (`/v1/images/{hash}`), NOT a bare hash.

Every other browse DTO does the same, and the client's `imageUrl()` prefixes the Hub base
onto whatever it is given — hand it a hash and it builds `https://hub/<hash>`, which 404s
silently as a broken image rather than as an error.

subtitle.description: Artist for an album/track, absent for an artist.

AdminUserDetail.description:
One row of the admin roster, with everything the table shows.

Separate from [`AdminUserRow`] rather than an extension of it: that shape is also what the
suspend/delete flows round-trip, and widening it would make every one of those carry seven
columns they do not use.

oneOf.description:
Last time any of this account's sessions was used. Absent for an account that has never
signed in since sessions were tracked.

AdminUserLibrary.description: A library this account owns, and whether its server is reachable.

AdminUserPage.description:
A page of the roster, plus the total the filters match.

Offset paging here, not keyset: the roster is small, sortable by any column, and an admin
genuinely wants "page 3 of 7" — the properties that made keyset right for the audit log are all
absent.

AdminUserProfile.description: Everything the user-detail page renders, in one request.

active_days.description:
Distinct days with any listening at all — a better read of "is this account used" than a
play count, which one long weekend can inflate.

badges.description:
Every badge this account carries, assignable or not.

The full list rather than just the two an admin can change, because the derived ones are
context an admin needs: whether someone is already a paying supporter changes whether comping
them a staff role is generous or redundant. The editor renders the assignable pair and shows
the rest as read-only.

ms_played.description: Total listening time, milliseconds. From the daily rollup, never the fact table.

oneOf.description:
The live admin comp, if this account has one. Shown so an admin can see what is already
granted before granting again, and so revoking has something to revoke.

recent_audit.description: This account's recent history as a TARGET of admin action, not as an actor.

AlbumArtistResolution.description:
The Hub's canonical primary artist for one synced album, so the library can organize files on disk
under the same name the Hub shows (e.g. a collab tagged "Wiz Khalifa & MGK" resolves to "mgk", and
"Machine Gun Kelly"/"MGK" fold to "mgk"). Keyed by the album's normalized title + the album-artist
name the library sent, which together identify the library's album row.

album_artist.description: The album-artist string the library sent (so it can match its own album row).

canonical_artist.description: The Hub's canonical primary-artist name for that album.

artist_image_url.description: The primary artist's image (for the breadcrumb / header artist chip). Framing-aware.

label.description: Canonical label display name (from the linked label entity, or a per-library override).

label_id.description: Canonical label id (for linking to the label page). None when unlabeled / override-only.

mbid.description:
MusicBrainz release-group id, when known. Mirrors `BrowseAlbum::mbid`, so a menu can link
straight to this release in the Manager rather than running a name search.

plays.description: Total plays across all tracks on this album.

secondary_types.description: Secondary release-group types (EP / Single / Compilation / Live / Remix / …).

AlbumEdition.description:
One edition of an album (Standard, Deluxe, Expanded, Remaster, …) with its own tracklist and
owned/missing breakdown.

is_remaster.description: True when this edition is a remaster (same songs, different master), shown independently.

owned_count.description: How many of them the user owns.

release_mbid.description: The representative release MBID for this edition.

tracks.description: This edition's tracklist in order, each flagged `owned`.

AlbumTrackCoverage.description:
Every edition of one album (release-group), each with its own tracklist + owned/missing breakdown.
This is the Manager's album view. Works for an album the user owns (to show which tracks/editions are
missing) and for one they don't own at all (everything missing).

artist_image_url.description: The album artist's image, for the breadcrumb avatar.

artist_mbid.description: The album artist's MusicBrainz id, for linking.

artist_name.description: The album artist's display name, for the breadcrumb trail and linking back to the artist.

editions.description: The album's editions, in display order (Standard first).

refreshing.description: True while the recording listing is still being fetched.

rg_mbid.description: The release-group MBID this breakdown is for.

ArtOption.description: One artwork candidate for the metadata-editor art picker (from fanart.tv / Cover Art Archive).

url.description: Direct image URL at the provider.

ArtOptions.description: Available artwork for an artist or album. These are the choices shown in the art picker.

ArtistCoverage.description: Owned-vs-missing breakdown for one artist the user (partially) owns.

artist_mbid.description: The artist's MusicBrainz id, if known (needed to diff the discography).

missing.description: Release-groups in the discography the user does NOT own.

owned.description: Albums the user owns (from their libraries).

refreshing.description:
True when the discography is still being fetched (missing list is provisional). The client
should refetch on the next realtime catalog nudge.

area.description: Where the artist is from (associated area / country region name).

banner_width.description:
Intrinsic pixel width of `banner_url`'s image, when the Hub knows it.

The banner is rendered edge-to-edge with a `srcSet`, and a `Nw` descriptor is a PROMISE about
the candidate's real width — the browser picks on that number without ever measuring the
file. Banner art comes from fanart.tv at whatever size the uploader chose, so a hard-coded
descriptor is a guess, and guessing high makes the browser choose a small file for a wide
slot and upscale it. Absent means "unknown": emit no `srcSet` rather than an invented one.

begin_date.description: Career/life start, raw MB partial date (`YYYY` | `YYYY-MM` | `YYYY-MM-DD`).

ended.description: True when the artist's life-span has ended (group disbanded / person deceased).

labels.description: Labels this artist has released on, with the year span (derived from their albums).

links.description:
External links (official site, streaming, social) from MusicBrainz, curated to the platforms
worth surfacing. Rendered as icon links on the artist page.

live_track_count.description:
Owned live material for this artist (live-version album tracks + scattered "(Live)" bonus
variants), so the client can offer the dynamic Live album even when no live album exists.

mbid.description:
MusicBrainz id, when known. Lets a menu link straight to the artist's Manager discography
page instead of dropping the user into a name search. Mirrors `BrowseArtist::mbid`.

monthly_listeners.description: Distinct listeners across the Hub in the last ~30 days.

related.description: Linked artists such as aliases, side-projects, or bands (see [`ArtistRelation`]).

ArtistLabel.description: A label an artist has released on, with the span of years (for the artist-page label history).

first_year.description: Earliest / latest release year on this label (either may be None if no dates are known).

ArtistLink.description:
One external link for an artist. `kind` is a stable platform slug the UI maps to an icon:
`website`, `spotify`, `apple_music`, `youtube`, `youtube_music`, `soundcloud`, `bandcamp`,
`tidal`, `deezer`, `instagram`, `twitter`, `tiktok`, `facebook`, `wikipedia`.

image_hash.description: Hash of an image uploaded via `POST /v1/images`.

ArtistRef.description: A reference to one artist (for rendering a track's per-artist links).

image_url.description:
The artist's own picture, as a Hub-relative `/v1/images/{hash}` path.

Here rather than fetched on demand because of where these are used: an artist reference is
what a track row and the player bar have, and both attach that artist's context menu, whose
header shows the thing you are acting on. Without the picture on the wire every one of those
menus fell back to a monogram while the same artist's menu opened from a card showed a photo
— and the hook that builds the menu runs for every row, so fetching it there would be one
request per visible track.

ArtistRelation.description:
One artist linked to another (an alias / side-project / band membership). Rendered as a
clickable chip on the artist page; each row is a real, independent artist (never a merge).

relation.description:
Coarse bucket the UI groups by: `"alias"` (also-known-as / pseudonym), `"member"` (band
membership, either direction), or `"related"` (collaboration / other).

Audience.description:
Who may see one profile surface. Used for the per-surface visibility knobs in
[`UserSettings`].

**A ladder, and each rung includes the ones below it**: `Private` < `Friends` < `Followers` <
`Public`. So `Followers` admits followers *and* friends, and `Public` admits anyone signed in.

The order is deliberate and is the opposite of set size in the underlying graph. Friendship is
mutual consent and following is one-directional, so neither group strictly contains the other —
someone can follow you without being a friend, and a friend need never have followed you. Placing
`Friends` tighter treats the closer relationship as the narrower audience, which is what the
setting reads as, and matches how the older `scrobble_privacy` `friends` value already behaves.

Anything wider is an explicit choice: the default is `Private`.

`Public` means *any signed-in account*, not the open internet — every one of these surfaces sits
behind authentication.

Shape-similar to [`ScrobblePrivacy`], which has no `Followers` rung; see the note there for why
the two must not be merged.

AudioProperties.description: Audio stream characteristics, captured at scan time.

gain_db.description:
ReplayGain 2.0 track gain in dB (reference −18 LUFS), computed by the loudness pass. `None`
until analyzed (or if ffmpeg/EBU R128 analysis is unavailable). The client applies it as a
preamp when "Normalize volume" is on.

lossless.description: Whether this is a lossless source.

peak.description:
Linear true-peak amplitude (≈0..1+), paired with `gain_db` to prevent clipping when applying
the gain (the applied gain is capped at `1/peak`).

spatial.description: Spatial/Atmos source, flagged `passthrough_only` and never transcoded.

AuditActor.description: An account that appears as an actor in the log.

AuditEntry.description:
One entry in the append-only privileged-action log.

`target_type` and `target_label` are what make an entry legible. A bare `target_id` is a UUID
with no way to resolve it — worse, `delete_user` destroys the row it points at, so after the fact
there is nothing left to resolve it *against*. The label is therefore captured at write time and
denormalized here on purpose; it is a record of what the target was called when the thing
happened, not a live lookup.

backfilled.description:
True when `target_type`/`target_label` were INFERRED by the migration rather than recorded.

Surfaced rather than hidden: a backfilled label is the target's name *today*, not its name
when the action happened, and for a deleted target there is no label at all. An operator
reading an old entry needs to know which kind they are looking at.

oneOf.description: The entity's relevant fields before and after the change, narrowed to what actually moved.

id.description: BIGSERIAL, strictly monotonic — which is what keyset pagination pages on.

target_image_url.description:
The target's art, resolved at READ time — unlike `target_label`, which is captured at write
time.

The distinction is deliberate. A label is identity and must be a record of what the thing was
called when the action happened; a picture is not identity, it is decoration that gets better
over time, and pinning a cover from the day of an edit would freeze whatever placeholder the
enrichment worker had reached by then. A deleted target simply has none.

AuditFacets.description:
The distinct values actually present in the log, for populating the filter dropdowns.

Derived from the data rather than from a hard-coded list, so an action added on the server shows
up in the filter without a matching client release — and one that has never fired does not
offer an empty filter.

AuditPage.description:
A page of the audit log, plus the cursor for the page after it.

Keyset, not offset: the log is append-only and unbounded, so an offset page shifts under the
reader every time anything privileged happens while they are looking at it.

next_before_id.description: Pass back as `before_id` for the next page. `None` means this was the last one.

AuthResponse.description: Response from register/login: the profile plus a fresh token pair.

BadgeCatalogEntry.description:
One badge in the instance's badge directory: what it is, who has it, and whether it is still
possible to get.

Deliberately keyed by the same `kind` strings [`ProfileBadge`] tags itself with, so the directory
and a badge on a profile are provably the same set — a badge that exists but is missing from the
directory would be the failure nobody notices.

oneOf.description: When the badge stops being obtainable, if that is a date. Only the early-bird badge has one.

history.description:
Cumulative holders over time, oldest first — one point per day on which the count changed.

Empty where the history is not recorded rather than estimated. A tier badge only knows when
its holder's CURRENT streak began, so a subscriber count for last March cannot be recovered
and is not invented; the client says so instead of drawing a line.

holders.description: How many accounts currently carry it.

obtainable.description:
Whether a new account could still earn it today.

False for the early-bird badge once its cutoff has passed, and for the early-supporter badge
once all hundred ranks are taken. The tier badges are always obtainable; the granted ones
(developer, staff) are obtainable only in the sense that an admin may grant them, which is
reported as false because it is not something a reader can go and do.

remaining.description: How many of a capped badge remain. Only the early-supporter badge is capped.

BadgeCountPoint.description: One point on a badge's holders-over-time line.

holders.description: Total holders as of the end of that day.

BillingMe.description: `GET /v1/billing/me`. The billing view of the account, beside its entitlements.

oneOf.description: When the current paid period ends: the renewal date, or the date access stops if cancelled.

has_customer.description: Whether a billing-portal link can be minted for this account.

oneOf.description:
A checkout started but not yet confirmed by a webhook, so the plan page can say "activating"
after a reload rather than looking like the payment did nothing.

BillingStatus.description:
The lifecycle state of a subscription, as far as the account is concerned.

`Canceled` is NOT the same as `Expired`: a canceled subscription keeps its entitlements until
the period already paid for runs out, which is the difference between "I turned off renewal" and
"I no longer have this".

BrowseAlbum.description: An album as shown in a grid.

album_type.description:
Primary release type (`Album`/`EP`/`Single`/`Compilation`/…), when known. Drives the
discography type badges.

appears_on.description:
True when this album is in the list only because the artist is a FEATURED credit on one of its
tracks (not the album's primary artist) — lets the discography mark "appears on" entries.

mbid.description:
MusicBrainz release-group MBID, when known. Lets the Manager link an owned album to its
coverage/tracklist view (which is keyed by release-group).

release_date.description:
First-release date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), when known. Used for precise newest-first ordering and
labels in the discography (finer than `year`).

version_type.description:
Version tag: absent for the studio release, "instrumental" / "live" for a version release, so
browsing can shelve them separately and Manager Discover can badge them.

BrowseArtist.description: An artist as shown in a grid.

mbid.description: MusicBrainz id, when known. Lets the Manager link an owned artist to its browse-all page.

BrowseTrack.description: A track row as shown in a list. `library_id` tells the player which library to stream from.

oneOf.description: When the track was added to the playlist / liked (epoch ms). None outside those contexts.

advisory.description:
Content advisory: `"explicit"` or `"clean"` (from the file's iTunes/ID3 rating tag), `None`
when unrated. Drives the EXPLICIT badge.

artist.description: Display string of all credited artists (e.g. `"Drake feat. Rihanna"`).

artist_id.description: Primary artist id (album attribution / "main artist" navigation).

artists.description:
All credited artists, ordered (primary first), for per-artist links. May be empty for
legacy rows synced before multi-artist support.

edition.description:
Edition qualifier ("Deluxe", …) when this track is from a deluxe/special edition folded into
the base album; `None` for the standard edition. Lets the album view badge the extra tracks.

library_id.description: The library this playable track lives in (for grant + streaming).

plays.description: Total times this track has been played (across the Hub).

track_ref.description: The library's own track id, used to build the stream URL.

variants.description:
Markers lifted out of the title on the way into the catalog: `Live`, `Remaster`, and so on.

The title above is what is LEFT once these are removed, so the two are read together: a row
shows the song's name and badges what kind of recording it is, instead of repeating
"(Album Version (Explicit))" down every line of an album. See `crate::variants`.

BucketGranularity.description: Grain the over-time series is bucketed at, so the client can label its x-axis correctly.

CapabilityAction.description: What a capability token authorizes the holder to do.

CapabilityClaims.description:
Claims inside a **capability token** - the linchpin of the data-plane security model.

Minted by the Hub only after verifying friendship + share permissions, then validated
**offline** by the target library against the Hub JWKS.

action.description: What may be done with it.

aud.description: Audience - the `server_id` of the library expected to honor this token.

jti.description: Unique token id - enables revocation lists and replay detection.

permission_level.description: Permission level granted to the subject for this library (owner → Download, shared → per-share).

room_id.description: Room context, set for relay tokens so the DJ's library can scope the grant.

sub.description: Subject - the user (or, for relay, the requesting library's owner) being authorized.

CatalogPruneRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/catalog/prune` (server-authenticated). The authoritative set of track refs the
library still has; the Hub drops memberships for any of this library's tracks not in the set, so
files deleted on the library side disappear from browsing.

library_id.description: The Hub-side library UUID this prune applies to.

track_refs.description: Every `track_ref` the library currently has for this library.

library_id.description: The Hub-side library UUID this catalog belongs to.

CatalogSyncResponse.description:
Response to a catalog sync: how many tracks were accepted and which referenced cover hashes the
Hub still needs the bytes for (upload via `PUT /v1/catalog/covers/{hash}`).

canonical_album_artists.description:
The Hub's canonical album-artist per album in this batch, so the library can file albums under
the same name (and relocate when it changes). Empty from older Hubs.

revoke_other_sessions.description:
Sign every other device out after the change. Defaults to true — the safe reading of a
password change is that the old one may be compromised.

ChangePlanRequest.description: `POST /v1/billing/change`: move an existing subscription to another tier or interval.

ChartEntry.description: One ranked catalog entry in a current-versus-previous-window chart.

ChartPage.description:
One page of a listener's full ranked library. Offset-paged rather than keyset: the ranking is
dense and recomputed per window, so there is no stable cursor to page from, and a reader jumping
to "page 7" expects ranks 121–140 rather than wherever a cursor happened to land.

total.description:
Distinct entities of this kind the listener played in the window — the denominator behind
"#7 of 412", and what tells the client whether another page exists.

checkout_url.description: Send the browser here. Hosted by the payment provider; card details never reach the Hub.

request_id.description: Our idempotency key, echoed back on the return URL so the page can poll for activation.

ClientMessage.description: Messages a client sends over the room WebSocket.

oneOf.description: DJ transport controls (ignored unless the sender is the current DJ).
Latency probe for room-clock synchronization (echoed back).

ClockGrid.description: Listening intensity by local weekday and hour.

cells.description: Exactly 168 row-major entries: `dow * 24 + hour`, with Sunday at row zero.

peak.description: Highest non-zero play count in any cell.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to place events into local calendar cells.

handle.description: Handle of the user to invite.

ColumnKind.description:
How a column should be rendered, decided server-side from what it actually holds.

The client cannot infer this: a `TEXT` column holding a sha256 and one holding a display name
are the same type on the wire, and only the table definition knows which is which.

Compared.description:
A figure measured against the equivalent preceding window, so a number can be read as a trend
rather than in isolation.

change.description:
Fractional change, for example `-0.73` for a 73% drop. `None` when `previous` is zero,
because percentage change from nothing is undefined; clients should describe this as
"new" rather than rendering infinity.

Compatibility.description:
Taste-compatibility between the caller and another user: a 0 to 1 overlap score plus the artists
they share. Only returned when the other user's privacy permits it.

score.description: Cosine similarity (0.0 to 1.0) over the two users' top-artist play vectors.

shared_artists.description: Artists both users have played, most-shared first (capped).

oneOf.description:
The detailed breakdown behind the score. Present only when the VIEWER's plan includes
`taste_match_summary`; omitted entirely otherwise, so the free shape is byte-identical to
what it was before the field existed.

CoverageSummary.description: Headline coverage across the libraries a user owns (and optionally those shared with them).

album_pct.description:
Album-level coverage: owned release-groups / total release-groups across touched artists
(0..100). The headline number.

artist_pct.description: Coarse artist-level coverage: artists fully owned / artists touched (0..100).

complete_artists.description: Of those, how many are fully owned (no missing release-groups).

excluded_library_ids.description: Libraries the user has excluded from this computation.

owned_rgs.description:
Release-groups owned across all touched artists (an artist is "touched" if the user owns at
least one of their tracks).

pending_artists.description: Artists still awaiting a discography fetch (coverage for them is provisional until fetched).

per_library.description: Per-library owned counts, in priority order.

total_rgs.description: Total release-groups across those artists (from the discography cache).

touched_artists.description: Artists with at least one owned track that the discography cache has been fetched for.

CreatePlaylistRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/playlists`.

Only `name` is required, and a body of `{"name": "…"}` behaves exactly as it did when that was
the whole shape — the two additions are `#[serde(default)]` so an older client keeps working.

They exist because creation used to be a one-field prompt, which meant the two decisions that
matter most about a playlist were made *after* it existed: a new playlist was public-by-default
in effect, since nobody visits a settings dialog to lock down something they just made. Asking
once, at the moment of naming, is both fewer steps and a safer default.

oneOf.description: Omitted means [`PlaylistVisibility::Private`] — the same thing the column defaults to.

DailyMix.description:
A "Made for you" daily mix, a generated station anchored on an artist the user plays. Playing it
runs the same radio generation as the artist's radio (`/discovery/radio?artist=seed_artist_id`).

seed_artist_id.description: Artist the mix is seeded from; play the mix by generating radio from this id.

subtitle.description: A few artist names featured in the mix, e.g. "Radiohead, Portishead and more".

DailyMixDetail.description: A daily mix opened as a playlist: its identity plus the generated track list.

seed_artist_name.description:
The seed artist's display name on its own.

`title` is already "<Artist> Radio" / "<Artist> Mix", and that is not decomposable in a
locale-safe way — so the breadcrumb trail cannot split it into `Artist > Radio` by trimming a
suffix. Carrying the bare name costs one field and avoids a second request.

DecadeBucket.description: Plays attributed to albums released in one decade.

decade.description: The decade's first year, for example `1990`.

DecadeSplit.description: One decade's plays, yours against theirs.

decade.description: The decade's first year, for example `1990`.

DesktopAuthorizeRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/auth/desktop/authorize` — hand the desktop app the session you already have.

The desktop app cannot see the website's session: different origin, different storage. So rather
than asking someone to sign in a second time, it opens the Hub's own web frontend, where they
are usually already signed in, and that page calls this to mint a one-time code for the account
it is signed in as. The code goes back over the `chordia://` deep link and is redeemed by
[`DesktopExchangeRequest`].

This is why the desktop app needs no sign-in method of its own. Whatever the website supports —
password, Discord, a second factor, something added later — is what the desktop app supports,
without knowing anything about any of it.

challenge.description: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the verifier the desktop app is holding.

DesktopAuthorizeResponse.description: The one-time code to hand back over the deep link. Worthless without the verifier.

DesktopDownload.description: One installer on the current release.

filename.description: The asset's own name, shown so somebody can check what they downloaded against the checksums.

url.description: An absolute URL on the release host. Not proxied.

DesktopExchangeRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/auth/desktop/exchange` — the last step of desktop sign-in.

The desktop app cannot receive the web flow's redirect, so its OAuth round-trip ends at a
`chordia://auth/callback` deep link. **Tokens must never travel in that URI**: any other program
on the machine can register the same custom scheme, and a session handed to the wrong one is the
whole account. So the deep link carries a code that is single-use, expires in a minute, and is
worthless on its own — this request trades it for real tokens.

`verifier` is what makes "worthless on its own" true. The app invents a high-entropy string
before opening the browser and sends only its SHA-256 to the Hub; the code is bound to that
hash. A rogue app that intercepts the deep link has the code but never saw the verifier, so the
exchange fails. (This is PKCE, applied to Chordia's own exchange rather than Discord's.)

code.description: The `code` query parameter from the `chordia://auth/callback` deep link.

verifier.description: The original secret whose SHA-256 was sent as `challenge` when the flow started.

DesktopPlatform.description:
Which installer this is.

Deliberately more specific than an operating system: Linux ships two formats and a person on
Debian wants the `.deb`, not a choice between two things called "Linux".

downloads.description:
Empty when the release host could not be reached. The page says so rather than rendering an
empty frame that reads as "there is no desktop app".

notes_url.description: The release page, for anyone who wants the notes or an asset this list does not name.

version.description: `0.1.5`, without a leading `v`. The same string the updater compares against.

DeviceNowPlaying.description:
The caller's OWN live now-playing entry.

This is what lets a signed-in browser say "playing on your phone" instead of "not playing": the
Hub already holds one ephemeral entry per user, and this hands the user back their own.

Not to be confused with [`crate::room::NowPlaying`], which is a listening-room broadcast, or with
[`FriendNowPlaying`], which is somebody else's.

device_id.description:
Which device reported it. `None` for a report that predates device ids - a client that
cannot attribute an entry must assume it is its own rather than claim a phantom device.

DiscoverArtist.description: An artist surfaced by browse-all discovery, with whether the user already owns them.

disambiguation.description: MusicBrainz disambiguation comment (e.g. "UK rock band"), to tell same-named artists apart.

following.description: Whether the user already follows this artist.

genres.description: Genres/tags (cached from MusicBrainz/Last.fm), for a "who is this" subtitle on the card.

owned.description: True when the user owns this artist in their accessible libraries.

owned_artist_id.description: The owned-catalog artist id (set only when owned), for linking into the owned artist page.

DiscoverReleaseGroup.description: A release-group surfaced by discovery / an artist's full discography, owned-tagged.

version_type.description:
"instrumental" / "live" version release (from the MB disambiguation / the `Live` secondary type),
so the discography can badge it and shelve it apart. Absent for the studio release.

DiscoverResults.description: Results of a browse-all search: matching artists and release-groups, owned-first.

DiscoveredTogether.description: Something both listeners first played in the same week.

item.description: Display name of the shared discovery (an artist).

month.description: The calendar month the shared first week falls in, `YYYY-MM`.

DiscoveryResult.description: A discovery hit when searching for people to add.

oneOf.description: Existing relationship to the searcher, if any.

DiscoveryStats.description: How many distinct catalog entities were played and newly discovered in a reporting window.

repeat_rate.description: Share of window plays whose track was heard before the window (`0.0..=1.0`).

Entitlements.description: Everything a client needs to decide what to show. Served with the profile.

billing_enabled.description:
False when this Hub has no payment provider configured. Everything is unlocked, and clients
must render no plan UI at all — a self-hoster should never see an upsell.

complimentary.description:
These entitlements come from an admin/staff comp rather than a payment. No badge is granted:
the tier badges mean "supporter", and comping one would make it mean nothing.

features.description: The capabilities this account actually has. Branch on this, not on `tier`.

oneOf.description:
The oldest timestamp history queries will return, derived from `retention_days`. Lets the UI
say "plays before this date are hidden" instead of silently showing a truncated chart.

Start of the current unbroken paid streak. Survives switching tier and switching interval,
and survives cancelling then resubscribing before the period runs out; resets only when the
subscription actually lapses.

retention_days.description: How far back listening history is readable, in days. `None` = no limit.

EntityBreakdown.description:
Page-only listening detail for one catalog entity. Kept separate from [`EntityStats`] so the
lightweight catalog-page panel does not wait on clock and top-list scans.

clock.description: When the caller listens to this entity, in their own timezone.

top_albums.description: An artist's albums by the caller's play count. Empty for album and track.

top_tracks.description:
The caller's most-played tracks of this entity: an album's or artist's tracks; empty when
the entity is a track.

EntityKind.description: Which kind of catalog entity a per-entity stats query is about.

EntityStats.description:
A user's personal listening stats for one catalog entity (artist/album/track). This is the data
behind the "your stats" panels on the catalog detail pages.

oneOf.description: First/last time the user played this entity (epoch millis). `None` if never played.

global_plays.description: Hub-wide all-time plays from the entity's global rollup. `None` until the rollup has a row.

rank.description:
1-based rank among the user's entities of this kind in the requested period. `None` if the
user has never played it in the period.

rank_total.description: Number of the user's played entities included in `rank`. `None` when `rank` is `None`.

scope.description:
Whose plays these figures cover. Echoed back so a page can label itself honestly rather
than trusting the toggle it sent.

trend.description: Local-calendar play trend (chronological), for a sparkline.

EqBand.description: One parametric EQ band: a peaking filter at `freq` Hz with `gain` dB and quality factor `q`.

preamp.description: Pre-amplifier gain in dB applied before the bands.

ExclusionsUpdate.description: Replace the set of libraries excluded from coverage (body of `PUT /v1/manager/coverage/exclusions`).

ExplorerColumn.description: One column of a browsable table.

searchable.description: Whether the free-text filter searches this column.

sortable.description:
Whether `ORDER BY` accepts this column. Sorting an unindexed text column on a large table is
a sequential scan an operator did not ask for.

total.description:
Rows matching the filter, counted up to a cap.

Exact below the cap, because an operator paging to the end of a wrong estimate is worse than
the count. Capped above it, because an exact `count(*)` behind every keystroke of a filter is
a sequential scan the explorer has no business asking for.

total_capped.description: `total` hit the cap and the real figure is higher. Rendered as `10,000+`.

ExplorerRow.description:
One row, as display values.

Everything is a string (or absent for NULL) rather than a typed union: the explorer renders
values, it does not compute with them, and a `Vec<serde_json::Value>` would put `any` in the
TypeScript for no gain. `ColumnKind` already says how to draw each one.

id.description: Primary key, for the detail view and for React keys.

ExplorerTable.description: A table the explorer will show, and what it looks like.

image_column.description: The image column, when the table has one.

key.description: The key the API takes. Never a raw table name from the caller.

row_count.description:
How many rows, counted up to a cap rather than estimated.

This was `reltuples`, the planner's estimate, and it was wrong in the way estimates are
always wrong at small scale: `reltuples` is -1 until ANALYZE has run on the table, so a
three-row table reported zero. An operator cannot tell a real zero from an unanalyzed one,
which makes the whole figure worthless. A capped count is exact where it matters and honest
where it stops.

row_count_capped.description: `row_count` hit the cap and the real figure is higher.

size_bytes.description: What the table costs on disk, indexes and TOAST included.

title_column.description: The column whose value titles a row in the detail view.

ExtArtistDetail.description: A not-necessarily-owned artist's page in discovery: identity + full discography, owned-overlaid.

bio.description: Short artist biography (cached from Last.fm), shown on the external artist page.

catalog_artist_id.description:
The catalog `artists` row this discovered artist resolves to (created on demand). Editable via
the normal admin metadata tools; this is how Manager artist metadata is modified.

refreshing.description: True while the discography is still being fetched from MusicBrainz (list is provisional).

ExtRecording.description: One recording (track) in a cached release-group's listing.

owned.description: Whether the user owns this track (matched by recording MBID, or title + duration ±2s).

ExtReleaseGroup.description: A release-group from an artist's discography cache (may be owned or missing).

cover_url.description: Cover Art Archive cover, if fetched (Hub-relative image URL).

first_release_date.description: First release date, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (may be a partial date padded to the 1st).

secondary_types.description: secondary-types (`"Live"`, `"Compilation"`, …) the UI can filter on.

Feature.description:
A capability an account may or may not have.

Deliberately a flat list rather than a tier comparison at the call site: `has(SmartPlaylists)`
survives a tier being renamed, split or comped, where `tier >= Sonic` does not.

Fingerprint.description: Five normalized measures of listening behaviour over one local-calendar reporting window.

concentration.description:
Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index of resolved artist play shares:
`(HHI - 1/n) / (1 - 1/n)`. `0.0` is an even split across the `n` artists and `1.0` is a
single artist; no resolved artists is `0.0`.

consistency.description:
`1 - Gini` of daily play counts across every calendar day in the window, including silent
days. `1.0` means every day has the same play count; an empty window is `0.0`.

discovery.description:
Distinct resolved artists, albums, and tracks first heard in the window divided by all
distinct resolved artists, albums, and tracks played in it. The three entity kinds share
one denominator; an empty denominator is `0.0`.

replay.description:
Resolved-track plays after that track's first play in the window divided by all resolved-
track plays in the window. `0.7` means 70% of resolved plays repeated a track already heard
during this window.

variance.description:
Population coefficient of variation of daily play counts, including silent days, mapped to
`CV / (1 + CV)`. `0.0` is identical volume every day; values approach `1.0` as day-to-day
volume becomes more volatile. An empty window is `0.0`.

FingerprintReport.description:
A user's listening fingerprint and, when available, the arithmetic mean of fingerprints for
Hub users with at least 20 plays in the same window.

oneOf.description: Omitted when no Hub user meets the minimum sample size; never synthesized.

FollowInput.description: Follow an artist / update a follow (body of `POST /v1/manager/follows`, `PATCH .../{mbid}`).

FollowPage.description: One page of a followers / following list.

next_offset.description: Offset to request next. `None` when this is the last page.

total.description: Total edges, so the header can show a count without walking every page.

FollowUser.description:
One row in a followers / following list, carrying the viewer's relationship to that account so
the row can render its own follow button without a second round trip.

is_friend.description: The viewer and this account are accepted friends.

FollowedArtist.description: A followed artist, as shown in the follows list.

FriendNowPlaying.description:
A friend's currently-playing track (for the live "Listening now" feed). Only friends whose
scrobble privacy allows it are included.

FriendRequest.description: Send a friend request by handle.

FriendScrobble.description: One entry in the friends' recent-activity feed, a play by a friend whose privacy allows it.

Friendship.description:
A friendship edge as returned by the Hub. `user_a` is always the lexicographically smaller id
so each undirected edge has a single canonical row.

requested_by.description: Who initiated the pending request (for UI: incoming vs outgoing).

GenreDetail.description:
A genre page: the artists, albums and tracks that carry it, ranked by plays across the hub —
the shape a listener expects from a tag page.

variants.description: Every spelling folded into this genre, so the page can be honest about what it merged.

GenreSummary.description:
One genre in the browse grid. Spellings are folded (see `slug`), so "hip hop", "Hip-Hop" and
"hip-hop" arrive as a single row.

image_url.description: Cover of the most-played album carrying this genre, as the tile's art.

name.description: The most common spelling among the folded variants, for display.

slug.description: Fold key: lowercased, non-alphanumerics collapsed to single spaces. The URL segment.

GenreTrend.description:
Exclusive album-genre shares over time. Albums may carry multiple genres; for a stacked chart,
each play is assigned once to the highest-ranked top genre on its album. Plays whose album has
none of the top genres, including unresolved albums and albums without genres, go to the
trailing literal `"other"` entry.

buckets.description:
Chronological buckets. Every `plays` vector is parallel to `genres` and sums to all plays in
that time bucket.

genres.description: Top album genres in descending whole-window play order, followed by `"other"`.

GenreTrendBucket.description: One local-calendar bucket of exclusive album-genre play counts.

plays.description: Counts parallel to [`GenreTrend::genres`], including its trailing `"other"` count.

GrantRequest.description:
Request a capability (or relay) token for a resource on a friend's / DJ's library
(`POST /v1/directory/grant`). The Hub checks friendship + share permissions before minting.

oneOf.description: What the token permits. Omit for [`CapabilityAction::StreamRead`].
What the token covers. Omit for the whole library, which is the ordinary streaming case.

room_id.description: Room context, required for relay grants.

GrantResponse.description: A minted capability token + the resolved server to present it to.

HeartbeatRequest.description:
Heartbeat a library posts to the Hub on a fixed interval to stay "online" and keep its
endpoint/fingerprint current (handles dynamic IPs).

next_interval_secs.description: Seconds until the next expected heartbeat (the reaper marks stale servers offline).

HistoryEntry.description: One entry in the full scrobble history feed.

event_id.description: The play event's idempotency id (also the keyset-pagination tiebreak).

track_id.description: Resolved catalog track id, if the play matched the catalog.

HistoryPage.description: A page of scrobble history, newest first, with a keyset cursor for the next page.

oneOf.description: Pass these back as `before_ms` / `before_id` to fetch the next page. Both `None` at the end.

HourSplit.description: One local hour of day's plays, yours against theirs.

IdentifyRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/catalog/identify`: one track's acoustic fingerprint plus whatever the file already
claims about itself.

The hints are not filters — the Hub always asks AcoustID about the fingerprint. They break ties
among the competing recordings a single AcoustID id can map to (one song appears on an album, a
deluxe edition, three compilations and a live record, each a different MusicBrainz recording with
a different track position). Matching the hinted album is the strongest of those signals: it is
what makes a FLAC and an MP3 of the same track converge on one `recording_mbid`. All three are
optional and are routinely absent — an untagged import with no ALBUM tag is precisely the case
this endpoint exists to rescue.

album.description:
The file's current ALBUM tag, if any. The strongest disambiguation hint when present, and the
one most often missing on the imports that need identifying.

artist.description: The file's current ARTIST tag, if any.

duration_ms.description:
Decoded duration in milliseconds, as reported by `fpcalc` alongside the fingerprint.

AcoustID matches on duration as well as fingerprint, so this must be the duration `fpcalc`
measured, not one read from a tag. Milliseconds to match every other duration in these
contracts; the Hub converts to the whole seconds AcoustID expects.

fingerprint.description:
The Chromaprint fingerprint as emitted by `fpcalc -json` (base64-ish, URL-safe).

A lossy acoustic hash of the decoded audio, **not audio** — see the module docs. This is the
only reason an identification request may leave the library host at all.

title.description: The file's current TITLE tag, if any.

IdentifyResponse.description:
Response of `POST /v1/catalog/identify`: the identity AcoustID and MusicBrainz agree on for a
fingerprint, as far as it could be resolved.

Only [`acoustid`](Self::acoustid) is guaranteed. Everything else is `None` when unresolved and is
omitted from the JSON entirely — see the module docs: absent means "not resolved", so a consumer
backfills (`COALESCE`) and never overwrites a known value with a blank. If AcoustID knows the
fingerprint but has no linked recording, an `IdentifyResponse` with only `acoustid` set is still
worth storing: the AcoustID id alone is the strongest own-copy match layer, since two encodings
of one recording share it.

acoustid.description:
The AcoustID id of the best-scoring match. Stable across encodings of the same recording,
which is what makes it the top layer of [`crate::catalog::TrackFingerprint`].

album.description:
Canonical album title of the matched release, from MusicBrainz rather than from the file.
This is the field that gives an `album_id IS NULL` import an album at all.

album_artist.description:
Artist credited for the matched *release* — the album artist, which on a compilation or a
split differs from the track's own artist.

disc_no.description: Medium (disc) position on the matched release (1-based).

recording_mbid.description:
MusicBrainz Recording id of the chosen recording. `None` when the AcoustID id has no linked
recording yet (a real and fairly common state for new or obscure releases).

release_mbid.description: MusicBrainz Release id of the matched release (the specific edition, not the release group).

title.description:
Canonical recording title from MusicBrainz. Useful even when the file has a TITLE tag, since
the canonical form is what other libraries will have normalized against.

track_no.description:
Track position on the matched release's medium (1-based). `None` when the release lists no
position for this recording.

year.description:
Release year of the matched release. `None` when MusicBrainz has no date, a partial date
without a year, or a year outside the representable range — the Hub drops such values rather
than truncating them into a plausible-looking wrong answer.

ImportJob.description:
One history-import job, as created by `POST /v1/me/imports` and polled from
`GET /v1/me/imports/{id}`.

The counters partition `total_rows`: every row in the file ends up imported, a duplicate of an
already-stored event, or skipped (sub-30-second Spotify plays, podcast rows, unparseable rows).
`matched_rows` counts, among the imported, those resolved to a catalog track; the rest are
stored with their artist/title text and match later if that music arrives.

duplicate_rows.description: Rows that were already present (same deterministic event id), so nothing was inserted.

error.description:
A stable failure code (`"malformed"`, `"internal"`, ...) when `status` is `Failed`; clients
localize it.

imported_rows.description: Rows inserted as new listening events so far.

matched_rows.description: Imported rows resolved to a track in a library the owner can access.

skipped_rows.description: Rows not worth importing: sub-30-second Spotify plays, podcast rows, unparseable rows.

total_rows.description: Rows found in the file. `0` until parsing finishes.

ImportJobStatus.description:
Lifecycle of an import job. Terminal states are `Done` and `Failed`; a client polls until it
reaches one.

ImportJobsResponse.description: `GET /v1/me/imports`: the caller's recent import jobs, newest first.

ImportSource.description:
Which service an uploaded history file came from.

Detected from the file's content server-side; a client may also state it explicitly
(`POST /v1/me/imports?source=`), which is validated against the content rather than trusted.

InstanceInfo.description:
What a Hub says about itself to a client that has not signed in — capability flags, plus enough
identity for the desktop app's hub picker.

Unauthenticated by necessity: the desktop app calls this on a URL the user has just typed, to
answer "is this a Chordia Hub, what do we call it, and does it do Discord" before there is any
account here to authenticate with. A 200 with this shape is itself the "yes, this is a Hub"
check.

accent.description:
The accent this deployment wears before a listener has chosen their own — a preset name or a
`#rrggbb`. `None` means the operator has not set one and the app's own default stands, which
is different from their choosing that colour: it keeps following the default if it changes.

Public because it themes the sign-in and landing screens, which nobody is signed in to.

billing_enabled.description:
Whether this deployment sells subscriptions. False on a self-hosted Hub with no payment
provider configured — which is the default, and where every client must render no pricing,
no plan tab and no upsell at all.

discord_client_id.description:
This deployment's Discord application id, when it has one.

Also its Rich Presence application id — Discord has one identifier for both, so the desktop
app publishes presence under whichever application the operator already configured for
sign-in rather than carrying a second one baked in at build time.

Public because it already is: this value appears in the query string of every OAuth
authorize URL a browser visits. The client *secret* is the confidential half and stays on
the Hub. Derived from the same config as `discord_oauth` above, so the two cannot disagree.

discord_oauth.description:
Whether "Continue with Discord" will work here. False when the operator never configured a
Discord app, and a button that leads to a 500 is worse than no button.

frontend_url.description:
The Hub's canonical **web** frontend. The desktop app anchors the links its users copy here,
because its own origin (`https://tauri.localhost`) means nothing to whoever receives one.

name.description:
Operator-facing name, shown in the desktop hub picker. Self-hosters run several, and "Hub"
three times is not a picker.

social_enabled.description: Whether the follow graph and public profiles are enabled on this instance.

version.description: Hub software version, for support and for a client that wants to warn about a stale server.

LabelDetail.description:
A label page: its identity, enriched metadata, and the albums released on it (within accessible
libraries).

former_names.description: Former names merged into this canonical label (e.g. "Warner Bros. Records" became "Warner Records").

founded.description: Founded / dissolved, raw MB partial dates (`YYYY` | `YYYY-MM` | `YYYY-MM-DD`).

LabelSummary.description: A music label in the browse-by-label index.

LastfmSessionRequest.description:
Body of `POST /v1/lastfm/session`: the single-use web-auth token from the Last.fm callback,
which the Hub exchanges (signed) for the user's permanent session key.

LastfmStatus.description: A user's Last.fm connection status, for the settings "Connections" section.

username.description: The connected Last.fm username, when connected.

LibraryCoverage.description: Owned counts for one library in the coverage scope.

excluded.description: Whether this library is currently excluded from coverage math.

owned.description: True when this library is owned by the user (false = shared-with-them).

LibraryOverrideSummary.description:
One override a library owner has set, as their settings page lists them.

The point of this shape is that the page could previously only ANSWER "what have I set on this
artist" and never "what have I set at all" — the editor was search-first, so an override you
forgot about was invisible until you went looking for the exact entity again.

fields.description:
Field names this override actually sets, so the row can say what was changed rather than
only that something was. Names match the override input fields (`title`, `year`, `genres`…).

id.description: The catalog entity the override applies to.

name.description: What it is called AFTER the override, so the row reads as the library actually shows it.

original_name.description:
The canonical name, present only when the override CHANGES it. Absent means the name is
inherited and the row is showing the catalog's own.

override_main.description: Whether this edit also takes over the global catalog.

LibraryShare.description: A share grant: which user may access which library, at what level.

LibrarySummary.description: Summary of a logical library as registered with the Hub.

icon.description: Optional Phosphor icon name chosen by the owner; None → default icon.

server_id.description: The self-hosted server (`server_id`) that physically hosts this library.

LikedArtist.description: One artist's share of the caller's liked songs.

liked.description:
Liked tracks credited to this artist. Deliberately not a play count — this list answers
"whose songs did you keep", which is a different ranking from "whose songs did you play".

LikedPoint.description: One month in the growth of the caller's liked songs.

total.description:
Liked tracks held at the END of that month.

Counted from the likes that are STILL IN PLACE, because an unlike leaves no record: the row
is deleted, so a song liked in March and unliked in April was never here as far as this can
tell. The line therefore reads "how your current collection accumulated", not "how many
songs you had liked at the time", and those are different questions with the same shape.

LikedStats.description:
The caller's liked songs in numbers, for the disclosure on the Liked Songs page.

Everything derived from listening honours the caller's retention floor, so the ratios below
describe the window their insights already show rather than quietly reaching past it.

oneOf.description: Oldest and newest like still in place.

history.description: Cumulative growth, one point per month from the first like to now.

liked_plays.description: The caller's plays across their liked tracks.

never_played.description: Liked tracks with no play on record in the window. "Saved for later" made countable.

played_liked.description:
How many of those they went on to like. With `played_tracks` at 0 the ratio is undefined,
which is why both numbers are sent rather than a percentage computed here.

played_tracks.description: Distinct tracks the caller has played inside the retention window.

top_artists.description: Artists best represented in the liked list.

total_duration_ms.description: Their combined length. `0` when none of them resolve to a catalog track with a duration.

unliked_favourites.description: The caller's most-played tracks that they have NOT liked — the songs the heart missed.

ListeningCharts.description:
Chart-oriented listening data for a period: an activity time series plus the listening-clock
(hour-of-day) and weekday distributions. Computed live from the partitioned fact table, scoped
to one user over a bounded window.

clock.description: Plays by local hour-of-day, exactly 24 entries (index = hour 0 to 23).

over_time.description:
Plays bucketed across the window, chronological. Daily for windows up to a year; monthly for
`Overall`. Doubles as a calendar-heatmap source at day granularity.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used for the local calendar window and time buckets.

weekday.description: Plays by local day-of-week, exactly 7 entries (index 0 = Sunday through 6 = Saturday).

ListeningEvent.description:
A single listening event. Created client-side with a UUIDv7 `event_id` so it doubles as the
**idempotency key** - replays/reinstalls never double-count.

artist.description:
Artist display string exactly as reported by the client. This is deliberately distinct from
`fingerprint.artist_norm`, which is only a fuzzy-matching key.

fingerprint.description: Identity of what was played (resolved to the canonical catalog server-side).

playlist_id.description: Playlist the track was played from, when the play originated in a playlist context.

room_id.description: Room the track was heard in, when applicable.

started_at.description: When playback started (epoch millis, client clock).

title.description:
Track title exactly as reported by the client. Optional for compatibility with older clients;
resolved events can fall back to the canonical catalog title.

ListeningRecords.description: Personal listening records and all-time milestones for one reporting window.

avg_plays_per_day.description: Mean plays per calendar day in the window, including silent days.

avg_plays_per_day_compared.description:
Current and previous averages rounded to the nearest whole play per day. The precise current
value remains available in `avg_plays_per_day`.

biggest_day_compared.description: Play count of the busiest local-calendar day in each window (zero when a window is empty).

day_stats_pending.description:
True when the day-grained figures could not be computed yet: the UTC report is served from
the daily rollup, and on a Hub whose aggregator has never completed a pass there is no
rollup to read. The streaks, `active_days`, the averages and `biggest_day` above are then
placeholders rather than facts, and a client should say "still being computed" instead of
rendering a zero-day history as if it were real. Sessions and milestones are unaffected
(they scan the fact table directly), as are non-UTC reports.

top_sessions.description: Longest sessions first, capped at ten.

ListeningSession.description: A continuous listening session, split after a 30-minute idle gap.

LiveAlbum.description:
A synthesized per-artist "Live" collection: every owned live-version album track plus owned
live bonus variants scattered across the artist's other releases. Not a real `albums` row —
keyed on the artist (like `DailyMixDetail` is keyed on its seed), so it always reflects the
current library. The client localizes the display title/subtitle.

source_album_count.description: Distinct source albums the tracks were drawn from (for the localized subtitle).

tracks.description: Ordered by source album date, then disc/track position.

LoginRequest.description: A credential request (email + password) against the Hub.

remember.description: When set, the Hub issues a long-lived ("remember me") refresh token.

Lyrics.description: Lyrics for a single track, as served by `GET /v1/lyrics/{track_id}`.

manually_edited.description: True when a user set/edited these lyrics by hand (the auto-fetcher won't overwrite them).

youtube_video_id.description: YouTube video id captured alongside the lyrics, for future video support. May be absent.

LyricsEditInput.description:
User-supplied lyrics edit (`PUT /v1/lyrics/{track_id}`). The body is raw text the server parses:
when `synced`, each line is LRC (`[mm:ss.xx] words`); otherwise lines are plain text.

synced.description: Whether `text` is timed LRC (`true`) or plain lines (`false`).

text.description: The lyrics body: LRC lines when `synced`, else one plain line per newline.

LyricsLine.description: One lyric line. `start_ms`/`end_ms` are present only for [`LyricsSyncType::LineSynced`].

start_ms.description: Line start offset from the top of the track, in milliseconds.

LyricsSyncType.description: Whether the lyric lines carry per-line timing.

default_library_id.description: Default library to scope Manager views to.

MatchQuery.description:
Own-copy lookup query (`GET /v1/tracks/match`). Any subset may be provided; the library tries
from strongest to weakest.

oneOf.description: Which fingerprint layer produced the hit, for telemetry and UX confidence.
The matched local track, if any.

MatchStrength.description: Which identity layer produced an own-copy hit.

Milestone.description: A notable ordinal play in a user's listening history.

NowPlaying.description:
The "now playing" descriptor broadcast to a room. Carries the full layered fingerprint so each
listener can run own-copy resolution locally.

dj_user_id.description: The DJ whose library is the relay source of truth.

title.description: Display metadata (so clients without an own-copy still render the track).

NowPlayingReport.description:
A client's report of what it's currently playing. It's ephemeral, held in memory on the Hub for
the live "Listening now" feed, never written to scrobble history.

device_id.description:
Stable, client-minted id for the device that sent this. Opaque to the Hub - it exists only so
a client can tell ITS OWN report apart from one sent by another of the user's devices.

One id per browser profile / app install, NOT per tab: tabs of the same browser already
coordinate over `BroadcastChannel`, and giving them separate ids would make one person look
like two devices playing at once.

device_label.description:
Human label for that device ("Chrome on Android"). Display only, and only ever shown back to
the user who sent it.

OnThisDay.description: Listening-history memories whose local date matches today's month and day.

OnThisDayYear.description: One past year's plays on today's local month and day.

entries.description: Newest-first sample of that day's plays.

OverrideKind.description: Which catalog table an override points at.

ticket.description:
The single-use credential, presented to the library server as a bearer token on its
`POST /v1/libraries/pair` call.

Period.description:
Aggregation window for a stats report. Mirrors the Last.fm-style windows: 7-day, 1/3/6/12
month, and all-time.

PermissionLevel.description: What a grantee may do with a shared library. Read-only for the MVP; `Download` is reserved.

PinKind.description:
Which catalog entity a pin points at. `Radio` is a generated artist station (the pin's `id` is
the seed artist's id); it resolves to a "{Artist} Radio" entry that opens the station page.

PinnedItem.description: A resolved pin (name + artwork) ready to render in the sidebar.

PlanInfo.description: One purchasable plan, for the pricing table.

monthly_price_cents.description: Minor units (cents), so no float ever touches a price.

monthly_product_id.description:
Absent when this Hub has not configured a product for that interval, which is also how a
client knows not to offer it.

PlanTier.description: A subscription tier. Ordered: every tier includes everything below it.

PlansResponse.description: `GET /v1/billing/plans`. Public: the pricing table is readable signed out.

free_retention_days.description:
How far back Free can read its own listening history, in days. `None` = no limit.

Here because Free is not in `plans`, and a comparison table still has to fill that cell. It
used to be hard-coded in the client, which is how it came to say one year while the server
had been giving everyone two since the window was widened. The prices on this response are
read from the server precisely so they cannot drift; the same has to be true of this.

plans.description: Paid plans only — Free is the absence of a subscription, not a product.

PlaybackSource.description:
Where the bytes the user heard came from. Stored so insights can distinguish personal
listening from room/relay listening.

auto_cover_urls.description:
Up to 4 distinct album covers from the playlist's tracks, for an auto mosaic when no
`cover_url` is set.

collaborative.description: Whether the playlist has any collaborators.

cover_url.description: User-set cover, if any. Takes precedence over `auto_cover_urls`.

owned.description: Whether the viewer owns this playlist (false = they collaborate on someone else's).

visibility.description: Who may see the playlist. Defaults to `Private` for payloads written before visibility existed.

can_edit.description: Whether the viewer may edit (add/remove tracks), as an owner or collaborator.

collaborators.description: Users the owner has invited to collaborate.

description.description: Optional free-text description shown under the title.

owned.description: Whether the viewer owns this playlist.

owner.description: The playlist's owner, resolved server-side so the header can credit and link them.

total_duration_ms.description: Sum of the durations behind `track_count` (milliseconds), on the same unfiltered basis.

track_count.description:
The playlist's REAL length, counted server-side over `playlist_tracks`. Deliberately not
`tracks.len()`: `tracks` is filtered to what the viewer can actually play.

visibility.description: Who may see the playlist. Defaults to `Private` for payloads written before visibility existed.

PlaylistPatch.description:
Partial update for `PATCH /v1/playlists/{id}`. Every field is optional; omitted fields are left
unchanged.

"Leave alone" vs. "clear" is expressed with an explicit `clear_description` flag rather than a
`Option<Option<String>>` + `deserialize_with = "double_option"`: a double Option round-trips
badly through ts-rs, which flattens it to `string | null` and loses the outer arm entirely, so
TypeScript callers cannot express the distinction the Rust type claims to make. A plain flag is
the same information in a shape both languages can actually spell.

clear_description.description: Set the description back to NULL. Takes precedence over `description`.

description.description: New description. Ignored when `clear_description` is set.

name.description: New name. Rejected server-side when it trims empty.

PlaylistStats.description:
Listening stats for one playlist, behind `GET /v1/playlists/{id}/stats`.

Deliberately its own type rather than a widened [`EntityKind`]: a playlist is not a catalog
entity, and the entity path switches exhaustively over the kind on both sides.

oneOf.description: First/last play attributed to this playlist (epoch millis). `None` if never played.

global_plays.description: Hub-wide all-time plays from the playlist's global rollup. `None` until the rollup has a row.

scope.description:
Whose plays these figures cover. Echoed back so a panel can label itself honestly rather
than trusting the toggle it sent.

top_tracks.description: Most-played tracks *from this playlist* in the window.

tracking_since.description:
When playlist attribution began (epoch millis). Plays recorded before this have no playlist
context and can never be attributed, so the UI must state the limitation.

trend.description: Local-calendar play trend (chronological), for a sparkline.

unique_listeners.description:
Distinct listeners in the window. Only meaningful — and only populated — for
`StatsScope::Global`; always `None` for `Me`.

PlaylistTrackOrder.description:
Body of `PUT /v1/playlists/{id}/tracks/order`: the complete track order, top to bottom.

Ids absent from the playlist are ignored; playlist tracks absent from this list keep their
current position.

PlaylistVisibility.description:
Who may see a playlist. `Unlisted` is link-only: not listed on the owner's profile, but
viewable by anyone who has the id.

PortalResponse.description:
`POST /v1/billing/portal`: a one-time link into the provider's customer portal, where cancelling,
resuming and payment methods live.

ProfileAccent.description: A profile's own colour, applied to that page only.

gradient.description: Two or more stops when the owner chose a gradient; empty otherwise.

primary.description:
A CSS colour. Already resolved: a time-varying accent is flattened, because a visitor's page
must not animate.

ProfileArtist.description:
An artist on a user's profile "followed artists" shelf. Identity is the MBID because a followed
artist need not exist in this Hub's catalog.

artist_id.description: Local catalog id when the artist resolves here, so the card can link internally.

ProfileBadge.description:
A badge on a profile.

Tagged by `kind` with the detail inline, rather than a flat struct of nullable fields: a badge's
detail is exactly what makes it that badge, and every renderer has to switch on the kind anyway.

oneOf.description:
The person who builds this. Title and tagline are configured per account, so it can say
something true rather than a generic label.

Joined before this instance's early-bird cutoff.
Granted to someone who has translated Chordia. `languages` is free text an admin fills in,
because the honest answer is a list of locales and there is no enum that survives contact
with regional variants.

position.description:
Where this account falls in the instance's sign-up order, counting from 1.

The join DATE alone answers "how long have you been here", which is the smaller half of
what an early badge is about — being early is a comparison, and without the position
there is nothing to compare against. Unlike an early-supporter rank this is derived, not
allocated: it is recomputed per read, so a deleted account ahead of you moves you up.

oneOf.description:
One of the first hundred accounts to ever start a paid subscription. Never revoked, and the
rank is never reissued — including after the holder deletes their account.

streak_months.description:
Whole months of the current unbroken streak. The client derives any visual stage from
this, so changing the stage thresholds needs no server deploy.

ProfileLink.description: One external link on a user's profile.

kind.description: Free-text kind (e.g. `bandcamp`, `website`), used to pick an icon. Unknown kinds render generically.

PublicProfile.description:
A user's shareable public listening profile. Listening stats are populated only when the viewer
is allowed to see them (per the target's scrobble privacy); otherwise `private` is true and the
lists are empty.

oneOf.description:
The accent this profile paints itself in for visitors, when the owner is entitled to it and
the viewer has not opted out of seeing other people's accents.

badges.description:
Badges this account carries. Present on the locked shell too: a badge is identity, like the
handle, and withholding it would make a moderator unrecognisable on exactly the profile where
knowing they are staff matters.

banner_url.description: Resolved banner image URL (the Hub image endpoint), when one is set.

can_follow.description:
Whether the viewer may follow this account (false when already following, when it is their
own profile, or when the target is not open to follows).

created_at.description: When the account was created (epoch millis).

followed_artists.description:
The user's followed artists, with the same `None` = not visible / `Some([])` = visible and
empty contract as `playlists`.

followers_visible.description: Whether the viewer may open the followers list.

following_visible.description: Whether the viewer may open the following list.

oneOf.description: Friendship edge between viewer and this account, when one exists.

hidden.description:
**The whole profile is withheld** — the viewer may not see this account at all, and every
field below is a placeholder rather than a fact.

Distinct from `private`, which walls only the listening activity. The two are different
walls with different copy: conflating them produces a page announcing "this profile is
private" while showing the person's bio, banner and links.

Explicit rather than inferred. The locked shell is a zeroed DTO, and a genuinely visible
profile can produce a byte-identical one — a new account with default settings, no bio and
no followers, or ANY profile on an instance with the social layer switched off. A client
guessing from field shape therefore walls real profiles, which is precisely the "client
decides visibility" mistake the rest of this DTO is shaped to prevent.

playlists.description:
The user's playlists. **The `Option` IS the visibility signal**: `None` means the viewer may
not see this surface at all (render nothing), `Some([])` means it is visible and empty
(render the empty state). The client never decides visibility — the server has already
applied `playlists_visibility` and each playlist's own `PlaylistVisibility`.

private.description:
True when the viewer may not see this user's **listening activity** — `total_plays`,
`top_artists`, `top_tracks` and `recent` are then empty. Kept under its original name for
compatibility; it says nothing about the profile's other surfaces, which carry their own
visibility signals below.

PublicUser.description: Minimal public view of a user. This is what friend discovery and room listings expose.

oneOf.description:
How to paint this user's name, when they have that perk and have left it on. Resolved by the
Hub rather than sent as "their tier", so a client can never render a flair the subject is not
entitled to, and never has to know the tier of everyone in a list.

QualityPreferences.description: Per-network-class playback preference, persisted client-side and synced to the Hub.

auto_downgrade.description: Step the tier down automatically when buffer health degrades (and back up on recovery).

QueueItem.description: A queued track waiting to be played.

RankMove.description: A ranked item whose position changed between adjacent reporting windows.

RankMovers.description: Current-window chart movement compared with the immediately preceding window.

RecentItem.description: One "Jump back in" card: a recently played album/artist or one of the user's playlists.

mbid.description:
MusicBrainz id of the album's release-group / the artist, when known. Carried so a menu on a
"Jump back in" card can link straight into the Manager instead of falling back to a name
search — the source rows already have it. Always None for playlists.

subtitle.description: Secondary line (e.g. the album's artist), when there is one.

RecentKind.description: What kind of entity a "jump back in" card points at.

RecentPlay.description: Lightweight "recently played" feed item for the home view.

album_id.description: Resolved album id, when the scrobble matched the catalog.

artist_id.description: Resolved primary artist id, when the scrobble matched the catalog.

event_id.description: The play event's idempotency id. Always present, so it is the stable list key.

image_url.description:
Catalog cover resolved like history rows: track cover first, then album cover, through the
Hub image endpoint.

track_id.description:
Resolved catalog track id, so the row can link to the track. `None` when the scrobble never
matched the catalog — which is why this cannot double as the list key.

RecompressState.description: What the backfill has done so far, and whether it is still going.

before_bytes.description: Bytes the processed images occupied before and after.

error.description:
Why the run stopped early, if it did. Shown to the operator rather than swallowed: a
backfill that quietly gives up looks exactly like one that finished.

finished.description: The run reached the end of the queue rather than being stopped.

processed.description: Images re-encoded so far in this run.

remaining.description: Oversized images still waiting, as of the last completed batch.
