running.description: A run is in flight. Poll while this is true.

skipped.description: Images looked at and left alone: already small enough, or they would not decode.

stopping.description: A stop was asked for and the current batch is finishing.

RelayRequest.description:
Request from a client to its **own** library to relay a track it does not own from the DJ's
library (the "Hybrid Relay" fallback).

dj_endpoint.description: Reachable base URL of the DJ's library (from the Hub directory).

dj_tls_fingerprint.description: TLS fingerprint to pin on the relay pull.

relay_token.description: Hub-minted relay capability token (audience = DJ library).

track_id.description: Track to fetch on the DJ's side.

library_ids.description: The caller's libraries in their new priority order (first = highest priority).

ResolvedServer.description: Result of resolving a server before initiating a direct stream.

authorized.description: True if the Hub also issued a capability token alongside this resolution.

ResourceRef.description: The resource a capability token is scoped to.

RoomState.description: Full room snapshot (sent on join, then kept current via deltas).

ScrobbleBatch.description:
A batch flush of buffered events (`POST /v1/scrobbles:batch`). Clients buffer offline and
flush on reconnect.

ScrobbleBatchResponse.description: Ingestion result. `accepted` + `duplicates` should equal the batch size.

rejected.description: Event ids rejected as malformed, if any.

ScrobbleEdit.description:
An owner's correction to one of their own listening events
(`PATCH /v1/scrobbles/{event_id}`, a Super-Sonic capability).

At least one field must be present. Re-attributing (`track_id`) rewrites the event's canonical
ids AND its denormalized display text together; moving it (`started_at`) may relocate the row
to a different monthly partition. Either way the rollups are repaired by exact recompute.

oneOf.description: Move the play to this start time (epoch millis, bounded to [2000-01-01, now + 5 min]).

track_id.description: Re-attribute the play to this track (must be in a library the caller can access).

ScrobblePrivacy.description:
Who may see a user's listening activity (recent-scrobble feed, top artists, taste
compatibility). Defaults to `Friends` so sharing is opt-in beyond one's friends.

**This IS the listening-history / top-artists visibility control** — enforced in
`backend/src/api/v1/insights.rs`. Do not add a separate `history_visibility` knob.

The duplication with [`Audience`] is DELIBERATE and the two must not be merged: this enum's TS
binding and its `scrobble_privacy` key in the stored `user_settings` JSONB payload are
load-bearing across the frontend and in SQL (`payload->>'scrobble_privacy'`).

ServerEndpoint.description: A library server's current reachability record in the Hub directory.

tls_fingerprint.description:
SHA-256 of the server's TLS leaf certificate (hex). Clients **pin** this, making
self-signed certs safe against MITM.

ServerMessage.description: Messages the `dj` service broadcasts to room clients.

oneOf.description: Full state on join.
Clock-sync echo: `client_time` round-trips so the client can compute offset/RTT.

SessionInfo.description: One active login session ("device"), as shown in account settings.

current.description: True for the session making this request.

last_used_at.description: Last time the session refreshed (epoch millis).

user_agent.description: Raw User-Agent captured at last refresh, for a human-readable device label.

ShareRequest.description: Create or update a share (Hub-side, requires an accepted friendship).

SimilarUser.description: A user who shares listening taste with the caller (for the "similar listeners" surface).

shared_artists.description: Count of artists both the caller and this user have played.

cover_hash.description:
Hash of an uploaded image, from `POST /v1/images` — the same upload a regular playlist's
cover uses. Same three-valued convention as the schedule: omitted leaves it alone on update,
`""` clears it back to the auto mosaic.

refresh_interval_minutes.description:
Minutes between automatic refreshes; `0` = never. Omitting it means "leave the schedule
alone" on update and "use the default" on create — NOT "never". A client that predates this
field must not be able to silently switch a playlist its owner scheduled back off.

refresh_on_complete.description: Re-resolve when the playlist is played to the end. Omitted leaves it alone.

SmartCondition.description: One rule: `<field> <op> <value>`. `value` is always a string; the Hub parses it per field.

oneOf.description: Scopes [`SmartField::MyPlays`] to a window. `None` means all time.

value2.description: Upper bound for [`SmartOp::Between`]; ignored by every other operator.

values.description:
Every value this rule accepts, matched as OR: `artist is A, B, C`. Empty means the rule is
the single `value` above, which is how every rule written before this field existed reads.

`value` is kept in sync with the first entry rather than being emptied, so a reader that
predates this field still resolves the rule to something sensible instead of to nothing.
Only the text fields use it; a numeric or date rule ignores it.

SmartField.description:
The track attribute a condition tests.

The first seven are catalog facts. The rest describe the CALLER's relationship with the track —
when it arrived, when they last played it, how often — which is what makes rules like "on repeat
this month" or "liked but not played in a year" expressible at all.

SmartMatch.description: Whether all conditions must match (AND) or any (OR).

SmartOp.description: How a condition compares the field to its value.

SmartPeriod.description:
A window of listening history, for [`SmartField::MyPlays`] and period-scoped sorting.

Calendar and rolling windows are separate variants rather than a day count because they answer
different questions and read from different places: a calendar month or year is served by the
monthly rollup tables, while a rolling window has to scan the events themselves.

oneOf.description: One calendar month, `YYYY-MM`.
One calendar year.
The last N days, counted back from now on each refresh.

auto_cover_urls.description:
Up to 4 distinct album covers from the current snapshot, for an auto mosaic when no
`cover_url` is set. Follows the rules, so it re-shuffles as the playlist does.

cover_url.description:
User-set cover, if any. Takes precedence over `auto_cover_urls`.

Deliberately the same pair of fields a regular [`crate::catalog::Playlist`] carries, rather
than the icon slug this used to be: a smart playlist is a playlist, and having one kind wear
a picture and the other a glyph made them read as different species in the same sidebar.

refresh_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between automatic refreshes; [`SMART_REFRESH_NEVER`] (`0`) = manual only.

refresh_on_complete.description:
Re-resolve the rules once the playlist has been played to the end, on top of any timed
schedule.

The point is a list that renews itself as you finish it rather than on a clock you have to
guess at: "on repeat this month" is most useful the moment you have heard all of it. It is
the CLIENT that reports this, because only the client knows a queue ran out, and only the
queue knows which playlist it came from.

oneOf.description:
When the snapshot was last successfully rebuilt. `None` = never resolved yet. A FAILED
refresh does not move this, so a stale stamp is a visible symptom rather than a lie.

track_count.description: Tracks in the current snapshot, without hydrating them.

SmartPlaylistDetail.description: A smart playlist with its materialised tracks.

refresh_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between automatic refreshes; [`SMART_REFRESH_NEVER`] (`0`) = manual only.

oneOf.description: When the snapshot was last successfully rebuilt. `None` = never resolved yet.

SmartPreview.description: `POST /v1/smart-playlists/preview`: what a rule set would produce, without saving it.

count.description:
Matching tracks, ignoring [`SmartRules::limit`] so the builder can warn that a limit is
cutting the result down.

count_capped.description: The count stopped at an internal ceiling, so it is a floor rather than an exact number.

sample.description: The first few matches in sort order.

SmartRefreshResult.description:
What one refresh actually changed. Returned by the manual refresh so the button can say
something true — including "nothing changed", which is a result and not a failure.

added.description: Tracks now in the playlist that were not in the previous snapshot.

removed.description: Tracks that were in the previous snapshot and no longer match.

SmartRules.description:
The full rule set for a smart playlist.

Every field added after the first version is `#[serde(default)]`, and the rules are stored as
JSONB — so a playlist saved by an older client still deserializes, unchanged, forever.

limit.description: Max tracks to resolve (clamped server-side). `None` = a sensible default.

oneOf.description:
The window [`SmartSort::MyPlaysInPeriod`] ranks within. Required by that sort and ignored by
every other.

SmartSort.description: Sort order for the resolved tracks.

SmartSortDir.description:
Sort direction. `None` on [`SmartRules::sort_dir`] means each sort's natural direction: A-Z for
title, largest or most recent first for everything else.

StaffRole.description: A staff member's role, shown on their badge so moderation actions have a face.

next_cursor.description:
Opaque continuation token, or `None` when the station is finite.

Stateless by construction: it encodes the day and an offset, so `/more` rebuilds the same
weave rather than reading a server-side session, and a retried request is idempotent.

seed_id.description: The seed's identifier. A **String**, not a Uuid: a genre station is seeded by a slug.

seed_name.description:
The seed's own name, unformatted.

Load-bearing rather than redundant with `title`. The server used to hard-code English titles
(`format!("{name} Mix")`), which no amount of client-side i18n could undo. Handing back the
raw name lets the client compose the title in the listener's language; `title` remains the
server's fallback for any consumer that will not.

StationFlavour.description:
Which way a station faces.

**Not a label on the same list.** `Radio` points outward: it weights novelty, admits tracks the
listener has never played, and is endless. `Mix` points inward: it draws only from artists the
listener already plays plus their liked tracks, and is finite and stable for the day. The two are
the same machinery with the affinity term's SIGN flipped, which is the whole distinction.

StationKind.description: What a station was seeded from. A genre seed is a slug, not an id — see [`Station::seed_id`].

StatsScope.description: Whose listening an entity page is reporting on.

Streak.description: One consecutive run of active listening days.

active.description: True when the run reaches today or yesterday in the requested timezone.

end_day.description: Last local calendar day in the run (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

start_day.description: First local calendar day in the run (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

StreamQuery.description:
Query params for the stream endpoint (`GET /v1/stream/{track_id}`). The `Range` header drives
byte positioning; this only selects the tier.

SyncTrack.description:
One track in a catalog sync push. Carries everything the Hub needs to materialize canonical
artist/album/track rows and to associate the track with the originating library.

advisory.description:
Content advisory from the file's iTunes/ID3 rating tag: `"explicit"` or `"clean"`; `None` when
unrated. Drives the EXPLICIT badge.

artist_mbid.description:
MusicBrainz id of the PRIMARY credited artist, from the file's `MusicBrainz Artist Id` tag.

Artist identity used to cross this wire as name strings alone, so the Hub could only match on
a name — and a name is not an identity. An album tagged with an artist's former name
normalizes to something the current row does not equal, so ingest missed it and minted a
duplicate; two different artists sharing a name collided the other way. The library had this
id all along (`artists.mbid`, from `metadata.rs`) and already ships it over a DIFFERENT wire
(`UpgradeProposal.artist_mbid`), so the omission here was a gap, not a data limitation.

Optional because plenty of files carry no MusicBrainz tags at all; when it is absent the Hub
falls back to the name matching it has always done.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the file bytes, the Hub's per-library track identity key.

cover_hash.description:
SHA-256 of the embedded cover art, if any. Bytes are uploaded separately (see
[`CatalogSyncResponse::missing_covers`]).

edition.description:
Edition qualifier ("Deluxe", "Special Edition", …) when this track comes from a deluxe/special
edition that folds into the base album. `None` for the standard edition.

track_ref.description: The library's own track id, used by the player to build the stream URL.

TasteSummary.description:
The paid deep-dive behind a compatibility score: what two listeners share, when they both
listen, and what they found at the same time. Every figure is bounded by each side's OWN
retention window — a paid viewer buys no reach into a free friend's hidden history.

decades.description:
Album-release decades, one entry per decade on a continuous axis from the earliest decade
either side has played through the latest.

discovered_together.description:
Artists whose first listen (week-grained) happened in the same week for both sides, with at
least 5 plays each, strongest shared interest first, top 5.

era_overlap.description:
Histogram intersection (0.0 to 1.0) of the two decade distributions: 1.0 means the same
era shares, 0.0 means no overlap at all. 0.0 when either side has no dated plays.

hours.description:
Plays by local hour of day over the trailing 90 days, exactly 24 entries (index = hour).
Each side's hours are measured in their own timezone — the comparison is "when in your day
do you each listen", not "are you awake at the same instant".

shared_albums.description:
Albums both have played, ranked by the smaller of the two play counts (`plays` carries that
shared strength), top 10.

shared_genres.description:
Album genres both have played. `id` is a stable hash of the genre name (genres aren't
catalog entities) and `image_url` is always absent.

shared_tracks.description: Tracks both have played, ranked and capped like `shared_albums`.

time_overlap.description: Histogram intersection (0.0 to 1.0) of the two hour-of-day distributions.

TimeBucket.description: One bucket in a time series of listening activity.

start.description: Inclusive start of the bucket (epoch millis, truncated in the requested timezone).

TokenPair.description:
Issued token pair. The refresh token is opaque (server-side rotation); the access token is a
JWT verifiable against the Hub JWKS.

TopItem.description: One ranked entry in a top-N list.

Track.description: A track DTO as served by a library's catalog API.

artist.description: Track artist (may differ from album artist on compilations).

TrackFingerprint.description:
Layered identity for a recording, from strongest to weakest. Lets the same song match across
different files/encodings during own-copy lookup in DJ rooms.

acoustid.description: AcoustID. A robust acoustic fingerprint that survives re-encoding. Preferred match.

artist_norm.description: Normalized metadata for the fuzzy fallback tuple.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the raw file bytes (hex). Used for exact-file matching and a bit-perfect integrity check.

TrackVariant.description:
One marker stripped from a title.

Ordered by how much it changes the recording: the first few are genuinely different performances
and the last few describe the release a track was on. That ordering is what the client renders
in, so the badge that matters most is the one nearest the title.

TranscodeTarget.description: Concrete encoding parameters a non-`Original` tier maps to (server transcode target).

Trending.description: Globally trending content over a recent window (by distinct-listener count, then plays).

UpdateInstanceSettings.description: What an admin is changing about the deployment itself. Omitted fields are left alone.

accent.description:
A preset name or a `#rrggbb`. Explicit `null` clears it and restores the app's own default,
which is why this is a nested Option rather than a plain one — "leave it alone" and "there
should not be one" are different instructions.

UpdateProfile.description: Profile fields the user can edit. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

banner_hash.description: Content hash of an uploaded banner image (from the Hub image endpoint), not a URL.

handle.description: New unique handle. Validated server-side; omitted leaves the handle unchanged.

links.description:
Full replacement list of profile links. Omitted leaves the existing links unchanged; an
empty vec clears them.

UserFlair.description:
The colour treatment for an entitled user's display name.

Always a resolved, static colour: the subject may have chosen an accent that cycles or follows
their artwork, but a name in someone else's follower list must not animate — that is a
permanently painting element in a list of hundreds, which is the exact cost this app has spent
sessions removing. Time-varying modes collapse to their current or first colour here.

gradient.description: Two or more stops when the user chose a gradient; empty otherwise.

UserProfile.description: Full profile for the authenticated user.

badges.description:
Badges shown beside this user's name. Identity, not billing: an account can carry a staff or
early-bird badge with no subscription at all.

email_verified.description:
Whether the account's email address has been confirmed. Defaults true so legacy/partial
payloads don't nag verified users.

entitlements.description:
What this account may do. Served here so a feature gate anywhere in the client is a property
read rather than its own request — and so a gate is impossible to get wrong by inferring a
tier from a badge or a price.

is_admin.description: Whether this user has site-admin access (the admin surface). Defaults false.

totp_enabled.description: Whether two-factor (TOTP) auth is enabled on the account.

UserSettings.description: Per-user application preferences. Every field has a default so older/partial blobs still parse.

accent.description:
Accent preset name, hue-ordered: `crimson`, `ember`, `amber`, `lime`, `green`, `teal`,
`blue`, `indigo`, `purple`, `magenta`, `pink`, or `default` — which is the default, and means
"follow this deployment's accent" (`InstanceInfo::accent`) rather than naming a colour. An
unrecognized value is used verbatim as a CSS colour.

accent_mode.description:
How the accent behaves over time. `Static` (the default) uses `accent` as-is; every other
mode needs [`crate::billing::Feature::DynamicAccent`], and the Hub serves `Static` to an
account that no longer has it rather than rewriting the stored choice — so the look comes
back intact if they resubscribe.

accent_palette.description:
The colours a non-static mode cycles or blends between, and the fallback for `Artwork` when a
track has no cover. Two to six CSS colours; ignored when `accent_mode` is `Static`.

accent_speed.description:
How fast the moving accent modes move. Ignored by [`AccentMode::Static`],
[`AccentMode::Gradient`] and [`AccentMode::Artwork`], none of which move on a timer.

crossfade_seconds.description:
Overlap-crossfade duration in seconds between consecutive tracks (`0` = off, the default, so
tracks change with the normal short handoff). Clamped to `0..=12` client-side; streaming
sources only (a crossfade needs the Web Audio graph). The frontend drives the dual-deck engine.

default_surface.description: Where the app opens by default: `app` or `library`.

email_notifications.description: Whether to receive transactional email notifications (e.g. a friend request). Default on.

eq_presets.description: The user's saved custom EQ presets.

followed_artists_visibility.description: Who may see the artists this user follows.

followers_visibility.description: Who may see the list of accounts following this user.

following_visibility.description: Who may see the list of accounts this user follows.

locale.description:
Preferred UI + email language as a locale code (e.g. `en`, `es`). Empty = follow the
request's `Accept-Language`. Drives server-originated text (errors, emails) and the client
UI; the frontend also mirrors it into the `chordia_locale` cookie so SSR's first paint agrees.

name_accent.description:
Paint this user's display name in their accent wherever it appears. Requires
[`crate::billing::Feature::NameAccent`]; on by default so the perk is visible the moment it
is bought rather than needing to be found.

open_to_follows.description: Whether other users may follow this account without asking. Default on.

playlists_visibility.description:
Who may see this user's public playlists on their profile. Defaults to `Private`: a
playlist's own `PlaylistVisibility` opts it in, this only widens the *shelf*.

preload_count.description:
How many upcoming queue tracks to prefetch in the background for seamless, gap-free
playback. `0` disables prefetch; clamped client-side. Prefetched audio outside the window is
evicted as the queue advances.

profile_visibility.description:
Who may see the user's profile page at all.

Defaults to `Private`. This is the front door — every other surface here is only reachable
once it has let the viewer through — so it is the one that has to be opened deliberately.

scrobble.description: Whether listens are scrobbled to the Hub.

scrobble_privacy.description: Who can see this user's listening activity in social insights.

show_profile_accents.description:
Whether OTHER people's profile accents apply while this user is viewing them. A viewer-side
opt-out, not a subject-side one: nobody should be stuck with a page colour they find
unreadable, and the person choosing the colour is not the person reading it.

streaming_quality.description:
Listener-selected quality tier (the streaming ceiling). Serializes as `original`, `high`,
`normal`, or `data_saver`.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used for calendar-based listening insights. Empty = follow the client.

WrappedReport.description:
A listening-insights report for a user over a period.

Computed live from the partitioned `listening_events` fact table, scoped to one user over a
bounded window. (This previously claimed to be served from precomputed rollups; it never was —
the fixed-grain rollups cannot answer an arbitrary rolling window precisely.)

decades.description: Continuous decade axis from the earliest dated album played through the current decade.

genre_trend.description: Album genres over the same local-calendar buckets used by listening charts.

timezone.description: IANA timezone used to align the current and preceding windows to local midnights.

top_genres.description:
Top genres by play count. `id` is a stable hash of the genre name (genres aren't catalog
entities), and `image_url` is always `None`.

undated_release_share.description: Share of plays whose album release date cannot be resolved (`0.0..=1.0`).

window_end.description: Exclusive end of the window (epoch millis).

window_start.description: Inclusive start of the window (epoch millis).

get.description:
`{table}` is a KEY into a hard-coded allow-list, never a relation name: an unknown key is a 404,
and a table nobody listed is not reachable however it is spelled.

`GET /v1/admin/images/recompress` — how the backfill is going.

post.description:
A backfill for everything written before the ingest cap existed, which on a real instance is
most of the table: art arrived at whatever size its source chose and was stored verbatim, so a
handful of multi-megabyte masters ended up dominating a database whose largest read is 1024
pixels wide.

It runs on the server, not in the browser. It started as a bounded batch with the loop belonging
to the caller, on the reasoning that something rewriting every row it touches should run while
someone is watching — but on a real table it takes long enough that "watching" means leaving one
browser tab open and not touching it, and navigating away silently abandoned the run. The
reasoning was right about supervision and wrong about where the loop lives: it is still started
by hand, still reports as it goes, and still stops on request.

Safe to stop at any point, and safe to lose: each image is independent, and one not reached yet
is simply still large. Nothing is remembered between runs because nothing needs to be — the work
queue is a query over `images`, so pressing start again resumes by definition.

**A rewritten row keeps its key.** `sha256` is a content address and re-encoding changes the
bytes, so after this the key is no longer a digest of what it stores. That is the deliberate
trade: the alternative is rewriting every `image_hash` reference across a dozen tables. Nothing
reads the key back to verify it — `upload_cover` checks a hash, but against the body a library
sends, not against storage — and new writes still hash what they store, so the invariant holds
going forward and only the backfilled rows are grandfathered.

Postgres does not return the disk on its own: run `VACUUM FULL images` (or pg_repack) after.
post.summary: `POST /v1/admin/images/recompress` — start the stored-art backfill.
`POST /v1/admin/images/recompress/stop` — finish the current batch and stop.

patch.description:
Only `developer` and `staff` are assignable. The other four are derived facts — a join date, a
row in the early-supporter ledger, a live subscription — and granting one by hand would turn it
from a fact into a claim, which is the entire value those badges have.

Three-valued per field: absent leaves it alone, `""` clears it, a value sets it. Without that,
removing a developer title would mean also restating the staff role in the same request.

post.description:
Called by the Hub's own web frontend, on a page the desktop app opened. The caller is
authenticated in the ordinary way, so there is no new trust here: someone who can already act as
this account is asking for a second, deliberately short-lived way in, on a machine they are
sitting at.

The challenge binds the code to the app that started the flow, exactly as in the OAuth path — a
code that reached the wrong program is useless without the verifier it never saw.

post.description:
Every failure is a flat `401`, deliberately: expired, already used, never existed, and "the
verifier does not match" are the same answer to a caller who should have all four right, and
telling them apart tells an attacker holding a stolen code which half they are missing.

`POST /v1/auth/email-change/request` starts changing the caller's email. Sends a confirmation

post.description:
This is how a client obtains the credential that lets it stream audio: the Hub verifies
ownership (or an accepted-friend share) and returns a short-lived EdDSA-signed token plus the
library server to present it to. The token goes to the library as `Authorization: Bearer
{token}`; the Hub never sees the audio bytes. Pin `server.tls_fingerprint` on the connection —
library servers commonly use self-signed certificates.

`resource` and `action` are optional: omitting them grants `stream_read` on the whole library.
`room_id` is only meaningful for relay grants. `recover_management` is owner-only.

get.description:
Restricted to the server's owner and to users holding a share on a library it hosts. It used to
take `AuthUser` and never consult it, so **any** signed-in user could resolve **any** server id
and read back its `endpoint`, `owner_id` and `tls_fingerprint` — i.e. enumerate the network
location of every user's home server, plus the fingerprint a client pins. Being signed in is not
a relationship with the server's owner.

`NotFound` rather than `Forbidden` for an unauthorized caller: distinguishing the two would turn
this back into an oracle for which server ids exist and who owns them.
